newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr holds above key supports, eyes upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr holds above key supports, eyes upside.

text.p: The U.S. dollar came under heavy pressure along with U.S. financial assets on the first trading session of 1997 but managed to hold above key support levels, thus preserving its upside, analysts said on Thursday.

In late Thursday trading, the dollar was quoted at 115.68/78 yes versus 116.03/13 late Tuesday in New York, at 1.5437/47 marks vs 1.5395/05 marks, and at 1.3475/85 Swiss francs vs 1.3395/05. There was no trading on New Year day.
The 1.5385-mark and 115.20-yen support levels did not give in though the 30-year Treasury bond lost more than a point and the Dow industrials piled up steep losses before rebounding.
Currency strategist David Durrant at I.D.E.A. said the "dollar took its cue from the Dow."

"With both bonds and stocks off, we saw some weakness in the dollar," Durrant added, while noting the downward move may be limited due to the fundamentals that remain negative for the yen across the board.

"The yen has a sort of particular twist to it, mainly if you see the Nikkei drop sharply. This could open the gateway for some problems in Japan," said Durrant who cited some anxiety in the marketplace about the resumption of trading in Tokyo next Monday after a full week of holiday.
Durrant said fresh yen weakness could prop up the European currencies, including at the dollar's expense, but still benefit dollar/yen.
"The yen scenario is unclear. We could see the dollar quite weaker against the mark and other European currencies but dollar/yen holding fairly well," Durrant added.
On dollar/yen, analysts said a six-day rising trendline is being tested at 115.70 and seems to hold -- leaving a chance for a new attack on 116.20 resistance.
On dollar/mark, there is no convincing downside unless the key 1.5290 level goes, they said.
Analysts also said dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss have decoupled, with dollar/Swiss providing an about 20-percent better return to investors than dollar/mark on similar moves.
Dollar/Swiss has gone through a first resistance at 1.3450 and is now eyeing 1.3515 for fresh impetus, they added.
Cable, after an expected correction, is in danger of retreating to $1.68 if attacks on the $1.70 level fail.
As for mark/yen, though obviously running out of steam, it may be just taking a breather before a new bull run at 75.35, experts predicted.
